new_entities.name: Hydrolysed collagen peptides
new_entities.description: Ingested hydrolysed collagen peptide supplements marketed for skin, nail, joint, or hair support.

new_entities.name: Nail brittleness
new_entities.description: Clinical brittleness of nails including cracking, chipping, roughness, and poor nail integrity.

edges.effect_quant: The direct nail-specific signal comes from a 25-participant open-label brittle-nail trial where collagen peptides increased nail growth rate by 12% and lowered broken-nail frequency by 42% over 24 weeks. A later placebo-controlled 85-woman study also found improved nail color and broader visible nail-aging markers, but the total evidence base is still small and beauty-supplement oriented.
edges.population: adult women using daily oral collagen peptide supplements for weeks to months to improve brittle or cosmetically aged nails
edges.mechanism: Collagen peptides may supply amino acid substrates and bioactive peptides that modestly support nail-plate structure and periungual matrix quality over time.
edges.summary: Hydrolysed collagen peptides have some human signal for brittle nails, but the evidence is still mostly cosmeceutical rather than mainstream dermatology-grade. The direction is favorable, yet confidence should stay moderate because trials are small and often industry-linked.
edges.caveats: Most studies evaluate composite beauty outcomes rather than isolated brittle-nail pathology. Effects are gradual and may partly reflect overall nail aging or cosmetic appearance rather than structural cure.

evidence.citation: HexselD et al 2017 J Cosmet Dermatol
evidence.notes: Oral supplementation with specific bioactive collagen peptides improves nail growth and reduces symptoms of brittle nails.

effect_quant.comparator: increase in nail growth rate over 24 weeks

evidence.citation: VleminckxS et al 2024 J Cosmet Dermatol
evidence.notes: Influence of collagen peptide supplementation on visible signs of skin and nail health and -aging in an East Asian population: A double blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial.
